description:
Search notes and logs and summarise thread activity. Returns absolute paths and metadata, never file bodies; use `notes cat` or a file reader to open a result.

Subcommands:
  notes [--thread T] [--type TYPE] [--text S] [--since D] [--until D] [--limit N] [--json] — find notes
  logs [--thread T] [--text S] [--since D] [--until D] [--limit N] [--json] — find daily logs
  activity [--thread T] [--since D] [--until D] [--json] — rank threads by what happened in the window (notes, logs and hours)
  overview THREAD [--since D] [--until D] [--limit N] [--json] — full picture of one thread
  stream [--thread T] [--kind K] [--text S] [--today] [--reverse] [--since D] [--until D] [--limit N] [--json] — every dated record merged into one timeline

Args:
  THREAD / --thread T: thread name, 'Kind/Name' or wikilink.
  D: YYYY-MM-DD. --since includes that date and later; --until includes that date and earlier.

Flags:
  notes:
    --type TYPE   note type, e.g. Meeting; case-insensitive
    --text S   case-insensitive literal match on topic and body
    --limit N   max results (default 20; 0 = all)
  logs:
    --text S   case-insensitive literal match on entry lines
    --limit N   max results (default 20; 0 = all)
  activity:
    --thread T   limit to one thread
  overview:
    --limit N   recent items to list (default 5; 0 = all)
  stream:
    --kind K   comma-separated subset of note, log, task, done, hours, payment, thread, person, pending (default all)
    --text S   case-insensitive literal match on thread and summary
    --today   today only; shorthand for --since and --until today
    --reverse   oldest first (default newest first)
    --limit N   max events (default 100; 0 = all)
  all subcommands:
    --json   JSON output

Examples:
  ["notes", "--thread", "Projects/SGB", "--type", "Meeting", "--since", "2026-09-01", "--json"]
  ["logs", "--text", "invoice", "--limit", "0"]
  ["overview", "Projects/SGB", "--json"]
  ["stream", "--today", "--kind", "task,done,note"]

Notes:
  Dates are the date the event happened (frontmatter timestamp), not the date the note was written (filename). The filename is used only when the timestamp is missing or malformed.
  Content kept only in hours entries is not searchable by --text.
  Exit 1: unknown value in --kind.
